newsitem.title: UK: StanChart 97 estimates trimmed on costs.
newsitem.headline: StanChart 97 estimates trimmed on costs.

text.p: Analysts said they are likely to trim their forecasts for Standard Chartered Plc's 1997 pretax profits after the bank said it would increase investment leading to a seven percent rise in costs this year.
Most analysts were expecting some additional rise in costs in 1997, compared with a two percent increase in 1996, but this was typically five percent.
"We were aware that there would be cost growth in 1997, so I had already assumed a five percent rise," said Hugh Pye, banking analyst at BZW.
Pye said the difference, some 20 million stg, would mean his estimate would be trimmed to 945 million stg and he remains an enthusiastic buyer of the shares.

Analysts were generally supportive of StanChart's strategy of going on the offensive in its key businesses at this stage, given that in many countries in its main Asia-Pacific franchise, the banking market is protected.
"They have a genuine opportunity in those markets," said Nick Collier , banking analyst at Morgan Stanley. "They have built up credibility by delivering on things they have promised before."
Pye said that StanChart shares were seriously undervalued by a market that seems to still rate them using domestic banking criteria.
"The Far East markets are not understood and Standard Chartered is still tainted by a domestic valuation," Pye added.
Collier, who has been going for 990 million stg profit in 1997 said he would trim his estimate but had not yet completed his figures.
Also looking at a downside move is John Leonard of Salomon Brothers who has been forecasting a 910 million stg pretax figure for this year.

Leonard agreed that the bank's strategy of investing in currently protected markets against the day when they will be more competitive made a lot of sense but said the shares were currently fairly valued.
